newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds fall on profit-taking with U.S..
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds fall on profit-taking with U.S..

text.p: Argentine bonds fell late Thursday, succumbing to a bout of profit-taking in the wake of softer U.S. Treasuries.
"There was some profit-taking but it was not heavy," said a trader at a local brokerage house. After two days of strong gains in the market, traders were expecting investors to book some profits.
The FRB Brady bond due 2005 fell 3/8 to 88-7/8, while the dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 dropped $0.25 to 125.05.
In the last three sessions, the FRB rose more than $2.

Another trader reckoned the market was likely to "firm again." The anticipated placement of Argentina's $2.0 billion global bond issue, split between a five- and a 20-year bond before the end of January, is seen maintaining a firm undertone, said traders.
Traders said activity remained busy Thursday.
In the money markets, call money rates rose to 5.53 percent from 5.48 percent.
